class="wp-block-paragraph">An attempt to improve the quality and reliablility of instrumentation used in guns, tanks and aircraft.</p><p class="wp-block-paragraph"></p><p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Industrial Clean Room</strong></p><p class="wp-block-paragraph">Semiconductor</p><p class="wp-block-paragraph">Cleanroom technoloty of paramount important to create and ideal semiconducting material and chemical purity. Any small imperfection can have a drastic effect on how the semiconducting material behaves due to the scale at which the materials are used.<br>This industry drives the state-of-the art clean room design, and this industry accounts for a significant number of all operating clean rooms.</p><p class="wp-block-paragraph">Pharmaceutical</p><p class="wp-block-paragraph">Cleanroom is an integral part of the manufacturing process required to produce sterile drug products, vaccines and bio-medical devices. Clean rooms control living particles that would produce undesirable bacterial growth in the preparation of biological, pharmaceutical, and other medical products as well as in genetic engineering research.</p><p class="wp-block-paragraph">Miscellaneous Applications</p><p class="wp-block-paragraph">Other uses include advanced materials research, laser and optic industries, microelectronices facility, paint room and some aseptic foods production. While hospital operating rooms can be considered clean spaces, their concern is to control types of contamination rather than the quantity of particles present.</p><p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>External Sources of Contamination</strong></p><p class="wp-block-paragraph">Primarily through the air conditioning system</p><p class="wp-block-paragraph">Infiltrate through building doors, windows, cracks</p><p class="wp-block-paragraph">Controlled primarily by 1. High efficiency filtration 2. Space pressuriation 3.Sealing of space penetrations</p><p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Internal Sources of Contamination</strong></p><p class="wp-block-paragraph">Largest source is from people</p><p class="wp-block-paragraph">Shedding of surfaces, process equipment and the process itself</p><p class="wp-block-paragraph">Controlled primarilly by 1. 									<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Choosing the right <a href="/">Chinese cleanroom</a> supplier is one of the most important decisions in any cleanroom project. Many buyers first compare prices, but low pricing alone does not guarantee cleanroom performance, compliance, or long-term reliability. A poorly designed or poorly installed cleanroom can lead to contamination risks, failed inspections, production delays, and costly rework.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Whether you are planning a china cleanroom facility for pharmaceutical production, medical devices, electronics, laboratories, or food processing, it is essential to evaluate suppliers based on engineering capability, manufacturing quality, compliance knowledge, and after-sales support. A reliable <a href="/cleanroom-project/">Chinese turn-key cleanroom</a> <a href="/cleanroom-project/">project</a> supplier should not only manufacture panels and equipment, but also understand airflow control, pressure differentials, material flow, personnel flow, and validation requirements.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This guide explains what buyers should check before choosing a dependable Chinese cleanroom supplier.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img decoding="async" style="width: 55px; height: 55px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-1.png" alt="" width="55" height="55" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>1. Define Your Cleanroom Requirements Clearly</strong></h3>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Before contacting any supplier, you should first define your technical and operational requirements. Clear input helps suppliers prepare an accurate design, quotation, and project scope. Vague requirements often lead to unsuitable layouts, budget overruns, and project delays.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Cleanroom Classification</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img decoding="async" style="width: 841px; height: 200px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-2.png" alt="" width="841" height="200" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Start by identifying the required cleanroom standard, such as ISO 14644 or GMP. The target cleanroom class affects filtration, air change rates, room pressure, airflow pattern, and testing requirements. For example, an ISO 8 cleanroom has very different design requirements from an ISO 5 or GMP critical area.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Industry Application</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="width: 840px; height: 201px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-3.png" alt="" width="840" height="201" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Different industries require different cleanroom solutions. Pharmaceutical cleanrooms may require GMP-focused layouts, smooth hygienic finishes, pressure cascade control, and validation support. Electronics cleanrooms may require tighter particle control and static protection. Food and laboratory cleanrooms may need specific hygiene zoning, washable surfaces, and controlled personnel entry.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Layout and Workflow</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="width: 428px; height: 351px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-4.png" alt="" width="428" height="351" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A supplier should also understand your room dimensions, process flow, equipment layout, and future expansion plans. A good cleanroom design is not just about walls and ceilings. It must also support efficient personnel movement, material transfer, maintenance access, and contamination control.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>2. Check Certifications and Compliance Knowledge</strong></h3>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A qualified Chinese cleanroom supplier should be able to demonstrate real knowledge of cleanroom compliance, not just mention standards in marketing materials.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>ISO and GMP Experience</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="width: 837px; height: 220px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-5.png" alt="" width="837" height="220" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ask whether the supplier has experience with ISO-classified and GMP-related cleanroom projects. They should understand how cleanroom classification affects room construction, HVAC design, filtration stages, and validation.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Material and Component Documentation</strong></h3>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A professional supplier should be able to provide technical documentation for cleanroom panels, doors, windows, HEPA filters, lighting, flooring, and HVAC components. These documents may include material specifications, certificates, datasheets, and test reports. Proper documentation is important for inspection, approval, and long-term traceability.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Testing and Validation Support</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="width: 453px; height: 385px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-6.png" alt="" width="453" height="385" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Reliable suppliers should also understand cleanroom testing and commissioning. Depending on the project, this may include particle count testing, airflow velocity measurement, pressure differential checks, temperature and humidity verification, illumination testing, and noise measurement. For regulated industries, validation support is a major advantage.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading">3. <strong>Review Real Project Experience</strong></h3>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="width: 841px; height: 221px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-7.png" alt="" width="841" height="221" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A supplier’s past projects can tell you far more than a product catalog. Cleanroom projects involve design coordination, manufacturing accuracy, logistics, site installation, and system commissioning. Experience matters.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Relevant </strong><strong>Industry Portfolio</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="width: 839px; height: 235px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-8.png" alt="" width="839" height="235" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Review the supplier’s project portfolio and check whether they have experience in industries similar to yours. A company that has delivered pharmaceutical, laboratory, medical device, food, or electronics cleanrooms is more likely to understand industry-specific requirements.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Project Scale and Complexity</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="width: 411px; height: 361px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-9.png" alt="" width="411" height="361" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">It is also important to know whether the supplier has handled projects of similar size and complexity. A company that can supply a small clean booth may not be capable of managing a full turnkey cleanroom with HVAC, utility coordination, and overseas installation.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Modular Project Capability</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">If you are evaluating a <a href="/">Chinese modular cleanroom manufacturer</a>, ask whether they have completed a similar modular cleanroom project in China or in export markets. Modular cleanrooms require accurate production, clean interfaces, fast installation, and the flexibility to expand later.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Client References</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="width: 840px; height: 268px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-10.png" alt="" width="840" height="268" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ask for client references, project photos, case studies, or installation records. These materials help verify whether the supplier has real delivery experience rather than only trading activity.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>4. Evaluate Factory and Manufacturing Capability</strong></h3>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">One of the biggest advantages of working with a Chinese cleanroom supplier can be manufacturing capacity, but buyers still need to verify whether the supplier has real in-house production control.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>In-House</strong><strong> Cleanroom</strong><strong> Panel Production</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">If the supplier produces cleanroom wall and ceiling panels in-house, this usually improves consistency and quality control. This is especially important when reviewing <a href="/china-cleanroom-panel/">cleanroom panels manufacture China</a> capability, because panel accuracy affects sealing, appearance, and installation speed.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>HVAC and Filtration Capability</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A cleanroom is not just a panel enclosure. Its performance depends heavily on HVAC design, filtration, airflow balance, and pressure control. Ask whether the supplier can provide AHU selection, ductwork planning, HEPA terminal layout, air change rate calculations, and pressure cascade design. A supplier without HVAC engineering capability may only be selling construction materials, not a full cleanroom solution.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Customization and Modular Design</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A strong supplier should be able to customize room size, panel type, windows, doors, return air walls, pass boxes, air showers, and equipment integration based on your layout. This is one of the main advantages of choosing a modular cleanroom manufacturer China with proven engineering support. Modular cleanroom capability is especially important if you may expand or adjust the facility in the future.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>5. Ask What Documents the Supplier Can Provide</strong></h3>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Professional documentation is often a clear sign that you are dealing with a serious cleanroom company.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A reliable Chinese cleanroom supplier should typically be able to provide documents such as:</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<ol class="wp-block-list" type="1">
<li style="list-style-type: none;">
<ol type="1"></ol>
</li>
</ol>
<p>1.  Cleanroom layout drawings</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>2.  Panel and material specifications</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>3.  HVAC schematic or airflow design basis</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>4.  Equipment datasheets</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>5.  BOQ or itemized quotation</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>6.  Installation drawings</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>7.  Operation and maintenance manuals</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>8.  Testing or commissioning records</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>9.  Material certificates and filter data</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">These documents are especially important in any <a href="/cleanroom-project/">china cleanroom turn-key project</a>, where owners, consultants, contractors, and inspectors may all need to review the same technical scope.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading">6. <strong>Assess Installation and Overseas Project Support</strong></h3>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="width: 841px; height: 185px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-11.png" alt="" width="841" height="185" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Even high-quality cleanroom materials can fail if installation is poor. Alignment errors, sealing defects, weak joint treatment, or improper HVAC balancing can affect cleanroom performance and compliance.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>On-Site Installation Team</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="width: 840px; height: 172px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-12.png" alt="" width="840" height="172" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Check whether the supplier has its own installation team or only outsources site work. Directly managed installation is often more reliable, especially for modular cleanrooms, air showers, pass boxes, doors, and ceiling systems that require precise assembly.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Commissioning and Handover</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A dependable supplier should support commissioning, system checks, and project handover. This is especially important for overseas projects, where clients may need remote guidance, installation supervision, or startup assistance.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>After-Sales Service</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Long-term support also matters. Ask whether the supplier can provide spare parts, filter replacement guidance, remote troubleshooting, maintenance recommendations, and technical support after project completion.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading">7. <strong>Compare Value, Not Just Price</strong></h3>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="width: 427px; height: 364px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-13.png" alt="" width="427" height="364" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Many buyers choose a Chinese cleanroom supplier because of cost advantages, but the lowest quotation is not always the best value. Some low-priced offers exclude important items such as HVAC, installation, commissioning, testing, or validation support.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Detailed Quotation Breakdown</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ask for itemized pricing that clearly separates cleanroom panels, doors, windows, HVAC systems, cleanroom equipment, installation, shipping, and optional services. A transparent quotation reduces the chance of hidden costs later.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Scope Definition</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Make sure the supplier clearly defines what is included and excluded. For example, does the quotation include only materials, or does it also include design, installation, commissioning, and validation assistance?</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Payment Terms and Milestones</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Professional suppliers usually offer structured payment milestones linked to project progress, manufacturing, shipment, and installation stages. Clear payment terms help protect both parties and reduce misunderstandings.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>8. Watch for Common Warning Signs</strong></h3>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Before selecting a Chinese cleanroom supplier, buyers should also watch for red flags.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Common warning signs include:</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<ol class="wp-block-list" type="1">
<li style="list-style-type: none;">
<ol type="1"></ol>
</li>
</ol>
<p>1.  No real factory or production photos</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>2.  No engineering team for HVAC and cleanroom design</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>3.  Very low prices with unclear scope</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>4.  Limited documentation or missing certificates</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>5.  No overseas project experience</p>
<p>6.  No testing or commissioning support</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>7.  No installation supervision capability</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>8.  Slow or unclear technical communication</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A reliable supplier should be transparent, technically responsive, and able to explain solutions clearly.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h3 class="wp-block-heading">9. <strong>Questions Buyers Should Ask Before Ordering</strong></h3>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<figure><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="width: 839px; height: 250px;" src="https://rvcleans.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-14.png" alt="" width="839" height="250" /></figure>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">To reduce project risk, buyers should ask a few practical questions before making a final decision:</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<ol class="wp-block-list">
<li style="list-style-type: none;">
<ol></ol>
</li>
</ol>
<p>1.  Have you completed projects similar to ours?</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>2.  Can you provide project photos or case studies?</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>3.  Do you manufacture cleanroom panels in-house?</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>4.  Can you design the HVAC system and airflow layout?</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>5.  What standards do your cleanrooms follow?</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>6.  Can you provide drawings, datasheets, and certificates?</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>7.  Do you support overseas installation or supervision?</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>8.  Can you assist with commissioning and cleanroom testing?</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>9.  What is included in your quotation?</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">These questions help identify whether the supplier is only selling products or can actually deliver a complete cleanroom solution.</p>
<p></p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Final Thoughts</strong></h2>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Choosing a reliable Chinese cleanroom supplier requires more than comparing prices. Buyers should evaluate technical capability, manufacturing control, compliance knowledge, documentation, installation support, and real project experience. A dependable supplier should be able to support your project from design and production to installation, commissioning, and long-term service.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">When selected carefully, a professional Chinese cleanroom supplier can offer strong manufacturing capacity, flexible modular solutions, competitive pricing, and dependable project delivery for international clients.</p>

<p><strong style="color: #333333; font-family: 'Open Sans Condensed'; font-size: 24px;">Frequently Asked Questions</strong></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Is it safe to buy a cleanroom from China?</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Yes, it can be safe and cost-effective if you choose a supplier with real factory capacity, technical documentation, project references, and installation support. The key is to verify engineering capability and project experience, not just compare price.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>How can I verify a Chinese cleanroom supplier?</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ask for factory photos, workshop videos, project case studies, technical drawings, product datasheets, material certificates, and client references. You should also check whether the supplier can explain HVAC design, cleanroom classification, and commissioning procedures clearly.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>What should a cleanroom quotation include?</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A professional quotation should clearly list cleanroom panels, doors, windows, HVAC systems, Power system, cleanroom equipment, optional installation, shipping, and commissioning scope. It should also explain what is included and excluded.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Why is HVAC expertise important when choosing a cleanroom supplier?</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A cleanroom depends on controlled airflow, filtration, pressure differentials, temperature, and humidity. Without proper HVAC design, even high-quality panels and equipment cannot deliver stable cleanroom performance.</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<h4 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Can a Chinese cleanroom supplier support overseas projects?</strong></h4>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Many experienced suppliers can support overseas projects through remote design coordination, factory production, shipment planning, installation supervision, commissioning support, and after-sales service. Buyers should confirm this capability before ordering. </p>

				<div class="elementor-widget-container">
									<p>With years of experience in cleanroom design and hundreds of successfully completed projects, RVCS can design and supply the best clean room HVAC systems, meeting both your requirements and budget.</p><p>RVCS design and construct the ideal cleanroom for specific product sensitivities and workflow considerations. The HVAC system is at the heart of the cleanroom. The HVAC system should not be overlooked given its central role. HVAC system is actually the most complex and important system of a cleanroom facility as the HVAC system is responsible for controlling air cleanliness, temperature, humidity, and pressure etc.</p><p>RVCS have cleanroom HVAC systems design knowledge of regulations, cleanliness level guidelines, airflow, room pressurization, temperature control, humidity control, and accounting of processes taking place inside.</p><p><strong>Please contact our project department for further inquiry:<br /></strong><a href="mailto:sales@rvcleans.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener">sales@rvcleans.com</a></p><p><span style="font-size: medium;"> </span></p>								</div>

categories: small ions, medium ions and large ions.Small ions are complexes composed of 3-12 molecules with basic charges; medium ions are complexes composed of about 100-1000 molecules, generally deposited on microparticles; large ions are composed of 106 molecules aggregated together the condensed nucleus.</p><p>Effects of negative ions in the air on the human body</p><p>In fact, negative ions are negatively charged molecules in the air, and negative oxygen ions are negatively charged oxygen molecules. produced by air ionization. In nature, there are many negative ions in the air of forests, waterfalls, and seaside. There is a tourist attraction in some city that is famous for its negative ions. The content of negative ions in the air is as high as 200,000-300,000/cm3.</p><p>Practice has proved that the negative ions in the air have certain physiological effects on the human body, which are manifested in: lowering blood pressure, inhibiting asthma, calming nerves, eliminating fatigue, enhancing the body’s immunity and antibacterial ability, making people feel refreshed and working efficiently. Experiments have shown that when the negative ions in the air come into contact with the respiratory organs, charge migration occurs and stimulates the organs. The lighter the ions, the stronger the activity, and the more obvious the stimulation to the organs. The result of this biological stimulation will provide the content of free oxygen in the human blood, which will increase the amount of carbon dioxide exhaled and oxygen inhaled by the human body, which means that it has certain benefits for the human body.</p><p>The air in the clean room is filtered by pre, medium and high efficiency filters, so the negative ions content in the clean room air is almost zero. It is also one reason why people feel uncomfortable in cleanrooms.</p><p>Therefore, negative ions are not only needed in daily life, but also in clean 									<p> </p><p>RV-Cleanroom System Shanghai Corp .Ltd. (RVCS) is a privacy conscious organization and is strongly committed to your right to privacy. This Privacy Statement defines the commitment of RVCS to protect the privacy of personal information that is collected or used in the course of conducting business. By submitting identifying data, a visitor to our Web site is agreeing to RVCSs use of such data as described in this privacy statement.</p><p><strong>I. RESUMES</strong><br />When you submit registration information and/or your resume,your information and your resume are hosted on our internal servers. If you apply for a job or elect to register with RVCS at this Web site, RVCS will be able to view your information and your resume, but no one else will be able to view them.</p><p>RVCS requests your personal information at these collection points and maintains the information on their server which will be accessed by RVCS only and no other third parties. RVCS believes that managing your career is a life-long process, and even after your information has been entered into the RVCS resume database, RVCS retains indefinitely all the information gathered about you in an effort to make your repeat use with RVCS more efficient, practical and relevant. You are able to correct or update your resume submitted to RVCS at any time by going to RVCS.com/contact us.</p><p><strong>II. POINT-OF-VIEW ARTICLES AND E-NEWSLETTERS</strong><br />RVCSs Use of the Information<br />We use the information we gather on the RVCS Web site for the purpose of fostering a positive user experience, delivering the services that we offer and, ultimately, to create opportunities. We may use your contact information that you provide in the website to contact you via telephone,e-mail,direct mail or other communications regarding profile fits, updates at the RVCS site, such as new RVCS opportunities and services which may be of interest to you, or for telemarketing purposes. Should you decide that you would no longer like to be contacted by RVCS, please notify RVCS and our best efforts will be used to remove you from our contact list. If you do not wish to receive future e-mails from RVCS, please reply to the RVCS e-mail solicitation by including “Unsubscribe” in the subject line. Accordingly, you should not receive similar e-mail solicitations from RVCS in the future.</p><p><strong>Disclosure of your Information to Others</strong><br />RVCS uses your information internally, with other RVCS-owned subsidiaries and affiliates, but does not disclose your personal information to third parties, except as set forth in the following subparagraphs.<br />We may disclose such information if legally required to do so, if requested to do so by a governmental entity or if we believe in good faith that such action is necessary to: (a) conform to legal requirements or comply with legal process; (b) protect the rights or property of RVCS or its affiliated companies; (c) prevent a crime or protect national security; or (d) protect the personal safety of users or the public.</p><p><strong>Passive Information Collection</strong><br />RVCS uses persistent “cookies” to help personalize and maximize your online experience and time online. The cookie indicates that a user has previously visited the RVCS site, tracks user content/navigation trends, provides customized user messages and prevents users from registering more than once. A cookie is a text file that is placed on your hard drive by a Web page server. Cookies are not used to run programs or deliver viruses to your computer. These cookies are uniquely assigned to your computer, and can only be read by a Web server in the domain that issued the cookie to you. You may have the ability to accept or decline cookies. Most Web browsers automatically accept cookies, but you can usually modify your browser setting to decline all cookies if you prefer. Alternatively, you may be able to modify your browser setting to notify you each time a cookie is tendered and permit you to accept or decline cookies on an individual basis. If you choose to decline cookies,however,that may hinder performance and negatively impact your experience on the RVCS Web site.</p><p>RVCS uses log files on JavaScriptTM to collect domain information, referral information, browser information, pages visited, content viewed, files downloaded, and time spent per page. This information is then forwarded to our outside vendor for analysis.</p><p>RVCS combines your personally identifiable information with passively collected information. For example, when a user registers for a point-of-view article under About Newsletters on RVCS. com, RVCS is able to determine who the user is (based on the user registration information) and where they came from (e.g. if the user clicked on a banner advertisement) and the specific article downloaded.<br />Security.</p><p>RVCS has implemented technical and organizational measures designed to secure your personal information, including firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems, secured servers and database security, from accidental loss and from unauthorized access, use, alteration or disclosure. We continually update our network to protect the confidentiality of our data. Due to constantly changing environments; however, we cannot guarantee that unauthorized third parties will never be able to defeat those measures or use your personal information for improper purposes.</p><p><strong>Children</strong><br />RVCS is not intended for children under 18 years of age. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 18.</p><p><strong>Changes to Privacy Statement</strong><br />If RVCS decides to change its Privacy Statement, we will post those changes here so that you will always know what information we gather, how we might use that information, and to whom we will disclose it. We welcome your comments concerning this Privacy Statement. If at any time you have questions or concerns about RVCSs Privacy Statement, or you believe that we have not adhered to this Statement, please contact us by e-mail at info@rvcleans.com. We will use commercially reasonable efforts to promptly determine and remedy the problem.</p>								</div>

		<h2 class="wp-block-heading">Privacy Policy</h2>


<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This privacy policy describes how we collect, use, and protect your personal information when you use our website and services.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">1. Information We Collect</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We collect information that you provide directly to us, such as when you create an account, make a purchase, or contact us for support. This may include your name, email address, mailing address, phone number, and payment information.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">2. How We Use Your Information</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We use the information we collect to:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Process and fulfill your orders</li>
<li>Send you order confirmations and updates</li>
<li>Respond to your comments and questions</li>
<li>Improve our website and services</li>
<li>Send you marketing communications (with your consent)</li>
</ul>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">3. Information Sharing</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We do not sell, trade, or rent your personal information to third parties. We may share your information with service providers who assist us in operating our website and conducting our business, as long as those parties agree to keep this information confidential.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">4. Data Security</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We implement appropriate security measures to protect your personal information against unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">5. Your Rights</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">You have the right to access, update, or delete your personal information at any time. You may also opt out of receiving marketing communications from us.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">6. Cookies</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We use cookies to enhance your experience on our website. You can choose to disable cookies through your browser settings, though this may affect the functionality of the site.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">7. Changes to This Policy</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We may update this privacy policy from time to time. We will notify you of any changes by posting the new policy on this page.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">8. Contact Us</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy, please contact us.</p>
